descriptionChirho: The Hebrew proper name Elyoenai (אֶלְיוֹעֵינַי, meaning 'my eyes are toward God'), borne by several individuals in the genealogical records of 1 Chronicles and Ezra-Nehemiah. All 7 occurrences refer to the same proper noun across grammatical contexts: nominative forms (eng: Elyo'enai/Elyoeynai, arb: أَليوعيناي / أَلِيُوعِينَايُ, kor: 엘료에내, swa: Elioenai/Elyoenai/Eliehoenai), and conjunctive 'and Elyoenai' (arb: وَ–أَليوعيناي, spa: y–Elyoenai, hin: और–एल्योएनै). The slight spelling variations (Elioenai, Eliehoenai) in target languages are transliteration differences, not semantic distinctions.
